docs.title: ✨ Key Features
docs.text:
🧠 Advanced AI Perception

State-of-the-art object detection with YOLOv8 and NanoOWL, optimized for real-time inference on Jetson hardware with TensorRT acceleration.

🗺️ Real-time SLAM

Visual-inertial odometry with 3D reconstruction, path planning using A* and RRT* algorithms, and dynamic obstacle avoidance.

📡 Multi-sensor Fusion

Seamless integration of cameras, LIDAR, IMU, and GPS sensors with synchronized data processing and advanced sensor calibration.

⚡ CUDA Acceleration

GPU-optimized computer vision pipeline with custom CUDA kernels for image processing, feature extraction, and neural network inference.

🌙 Night Vision

Thermal camera integration with AI-enhanced low-light performance for 24/7 autonomous operation in any lighting condition.

🚀 Production Ready

Complete deployment stack with Docker, Kubernetes, Helm charts, OTA updates, and comprehensive monitoring solutions.

docs.title: 🚀 Quick Start
docs.text:
Get up and running in minutes:

DockerNativeKubernetes Bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL

# Build and run with Docker
docker-compose up -d

# Access the system
ros2 launch jetbot_nanoowl bringup.launch.py
Bash
# Install ROS2 Humble
sudo apt update
sudo apt install ros-humble-desktop

# Clone and build
git clone https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
colcon build --symlink-install

# Source and launch
source install/setup.bash
ros2 launch jetbot_nanoowl bringup.launch.py
Bash
# Install with Helm
helm repo add tng-blue https://tng-blue.github.io/charts
helm install jetbot-nanoowl tng-blue/jetbot-nanoowl

# Check status
kubectl get pods -n robotics

docs.title: How to Ask Good Questions
docs.text:
Writing Effective Questions

  • Be specific: Include error messages, code snippets, and system info
  • Show what you've tried: Demonstrate your debugging efforts
  • Provide context: Explain what you're trying to achieve
  • Use code blocks: Format code properly for readability
  • Include versions: Specify ROS2, JetPack, and library versions

Example of a good question:

Markdown

**Environment:**
- Jetson Orin Nano 8GB
- JetPack 5.1.2
- ROS2 Humble
- Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL v1.0.0

**Issue:**
Object detection node crashes with "CUDA out of memory" error after 5 minutes.

**What I've tried:**
- Reduced batch size from 8 to 4
- Lowered model resolution from 640x640 to 320x320
- Monitored GPU memory with nvidia-smi

**Error output:**
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 256.00 MiB Text Only
**Question:**
How can I further optimize GPU memory usage for long-running detection?

Yes, we offer professional support packages for enterprise users. Contact us for details.

What ROS2 version is required?

We officially support ROS2 Humble Hawksbill on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS.

docs.title: LoRa Packet Structure
docs.text:
Text Only
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Preamble │ Header │ Payload │ CRC │
│  8 bytes │ 2 bytes│ 0-255 B │ 2 B │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Header Format:
  - Device ID (1 byte)
  - Packet Type (1 byte)
    * 0x01: Telemetry
    * 0x02: Command
    * 0x03: Image Fragment
    * 0x04: ACK/NACK
    * 0x05: Heartbeat

Payload Examples:

    - Battery voltage
    - System status

  Image Transfer:
    - Fragment ID
    - Total fragments
    - Image data (200 bytes)

# Traffic shaping with tc (traffic control)

# Create root qdisc
tc qdisc add dev wlan0 root handle 1: htb default 30

# Add classes with bandwidth limits
tc class add dev wlan0 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 100mbit

# High priority: Control commands (30% bandwidth)
tc class add dev wlan0 parent 1:1 classid 1:10 htb rate 30mbit ceil 50mbit prio 1

# Medium priority: Sensor data (50% bandwidth)
tc class add dev wlan0 parent 1:1 classid 1:20 htb rate 50mbit ceil 80mbit prio 2

# Low priority: Other traffic (20% bandwidth)
tc class add dev wlan0 parent 1:1 classid 1:30 htb rate 20mbit ceil 100mbit prio 3

# Add filters to classify traffic
tc filter add dev wlan0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 u32 \
  match ip dport 7400 0xffff flowid 1:10  # ROS2 control
tc filter add dev wlan0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 2 u32 \
  match ip dport 7420 0xffff flowid 1:20  # ROS2 sensors

docs.text:
YAML
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: Continuous Integration

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Setup ROS2
        uses: ros-tooling/setup-ros@v0.6
        with:
          required-ros-distributions: humble

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt update
          rosdep update
          rosdep install --from-paths . -y --ignore-src

      - name: Build
        run: |
          source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
          colcon build --symlink-install

      - name: Test
        run: |
          source install/setup.bash
          colcon test
          colcon test-result --verbose

      - name: Coverage
        run: |
          lcov --capture --directory . --output-file coverage.info
          lcov --remove coverage.info '/usr/*' --output-file coverage.info
          lcov --list coverage.info

      - name: Upload coverage
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3
        with:
          files: ./coverage.info

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text:
The Object Detection module provides state-of-the-art real-time object detection capabilities optimized for NVIDIA Jetson hardware.

Key Features: - YOLOv8 Nano/Small/Medium models - NanoOWL vision-language model - TensorRT INT8/FP16 optimization - 35+ FPS at 1280×720 resolution - 80+ COCO object categories - Custom model training support

docs.title: Detector Interface
YOLOv8 Example
🐍 Python API
docs.text:
Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from sensor_msgs.msg import Image
from vision_msgs.msg import Detection2DArray
from cv_bridge import CvBridge

class DetectionSubscriber(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('detection_subscriber')

        self.subscription = self.create_subscription(
            Detection2DArray,
            '/detection/objects',
            self.detection_callback,
            10
        )

        self.image_subscription = self.create_subscription(
            Image,
            '/detection/annotated_image',
            self.image_callback,
            10
        )

        self.bridge = CvBridge()

    def detection_callback(self, msg):
        self.get_logger().info(f'Received {len(msg.detections)} detections')

        for detection in msg.detections:
            for result in detection.results:
                class_id = result.hypothesis.class_id
                score = result.hypothesis.score
                bbox = detection.bbox

                self.get_logger().info(
                    f'  {class_id}: {score:.2f} at '
                    f'[{bbox.center.position.x:.0f}, '
                    f'{bbox.center.position.y:.0f}]'
                )

    def image_callback(self, msg):
        # Convert to OpenCV image
        cv_image = self.bridge.imgmsg_to_cv2(msg, desired_encoding='bgr8')

        # Display or save
        # cv2.imshow('Detections', cv_image)
        # cv2.waitKey(1)

def main():
    rclpy.init()
    node = DetectionSubscriber()

    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass

    node.destroy_node()
    rclpy.shutdown()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

docs.title: 📋 Installation Paths
docs.text:
We offer multiple installation methods:

🐳 Docker (Recommended)🔨 Native Installation☸️ Kubernetes

Best for: Quick setup, isolated environment, easy updates

Bash
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL

# Run with Docker Compose
docker-compose up -d

✅ Advantages: - Fastest setup time (~30 minutes) - No dependency conflicts - Easy rollback and updates - Consistent environment

⚠️ Considerations: - Requires ~10GB disk space - Slight performance overhead

Best for: Maximum performance, development work, custom modifications

Bash
# Install ROS2 Humble
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y ros-humble-desktop

# Clone and build
git clone https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
colcon build --symlink-install

✅ Advantages: - Best performance - Full system access - Easier debugging - No containerization overhead

⚠️ Considerations: - Longer setup time (~2 hours) - Potential dependency conflicts - Manual updates required

Best for: Multi-robot fleets, production deployments, scalability

Bash
# Add Helm repository
helm repo add tng-blue https://tng-blue.github.io/charts

# Install with Helm
helm install jetbot-nanoowl tng-blue/jetbot-nanoowl \
  --namespace robotics --create-namespace

✅ Advantages: - Production-ready orchestration - Easy scaling and updates - Built-in monitoring - High availability

⚠️ Considerations: - Complex initial setup - Requires K8s knowledge - Resource overhead

docs.title: ❓ Common Questions
docs.text:
What if I don't have all the hardware?

You can start with minimal hardware (Jetson + one camera) and add sensors gradually. Many features work with reduced sensor sets.

Can I use a different Jetson model?

Yes! The platform supports Jetson Nano, Xavier NX, and AGX Xavier. Performance will vary.

Do I need robotics experience?

Not required! Our tutorials start from basics. However, Linux familiarity is helpful.

What if I get stuck?

Check our Troubleshooting Guide or ask in GitHub Discussions.
